title: Tribunus Server UX — Terminal Dashboard, Model Management, CLI Ergonomics, and Developer Experience for Local Inference
context:
The on-device inference server market has converged on a set of UX conventions. Ollama sets the gold standard for CLI-first zero-friction model acquisition. LM Studio demonstrates what a desktop-first GPU-aware interface looks like. llama.cpp server and LocalAI prove that OpenAI API compatibility plus Swagger docs are table stakes. Caddy shows how a two-tier configuration model satisfies both novices and power users.

Tribunus has a structural advantage none of these competitors share: precompiled compute images with assessment evidence. This means Tribunus can display information other servers cannot — which backends were benchmarked, what won, what numerical precision was validated, and what compilation evidence backs every loaded model. Making that evidence visible transforms server UX from a commodity (everyone has an OpenAI-compatible API) into a differentiator.

This ADR defines the terminal dashboard, model management, CLI ergonomics, API surface, configuration model, error UX, and developer experience for the Tribunus inference server. It builds on completed research in inference-server-ux-research.md and is the final UX-layer companion to runtime-pipeline ADRs (0033–0040) that define what the server runs.
decision:
### 1. Single-Command Bootstrap (`tribunus run <model>`)

The primary entry point is `tribunus run <model>`, which downloads, compiles, loads, and serves a model in one command — Ollama-style. If the model is not found locally, Tribunus searches known catalogs (HuggingFace, GGUF registry, Tribunus model hub) and auto-discovers the best matching variant.

#### Resolution order
1. Check local compute image cache for an image matching `<model>` + current hardware fingerprint.
2. If not cached, search configured registries (default: HuggingFace for safetensors/GGUF, Tribunus hub for precompiled images).
3. If weights found but no compiled image exists, trigger automatic compilation with progress display.
4. Load compiled image into arena and begin serving.

#### Progress display during compilation

```
$ tribunus run gemma-3-12b-it

  Downloading... ████████████░░░░░░ 68% • 4.9/7.2 GB • 12 MB/s • ETA 3m 12s
  Compiling compute image...
    [assessment]     ✓ Hardware detected: Metal M1 Max, 32-core GPU, 32 GB unified
    [kernels]        ████████░░░░░░ 8/12 kernels benchmarked
    [memory]         ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ planning arena layout
    [weights]        ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ compressing to Q4_K_M
  ✓ gemma-3-12b-it compiled in 47s (12.1 GB compute image)
  ✓ Server ready on http://127.0.0.1:11434
  >> Interactive chat session started. Type /help for commands.
```

#### Error: Model not found
```
Error: model "llama-4-maverick" not found in catalog.

Similar models from catalog:
  • llama-3.3-70b-instruct  (available, 70B params)
  • llama-3.1-8b-instruct   (already installed on this machine)

Run 'tribunus search llama-4' to browse the catalog.
Run 'tribunus doctor' to verify system setup.
```

#### Interactive chat mode
`tribunus run <model>` without additional flags opens an interactive chat session. Slash commands:
- `/model <name>` — switch loaded model
- `/system <prompt>` — set system message
- `/clear` — reset conversation context
- `/save <file>` — export conversation to file
- `/params` — show current generation settings (temperature, top-p, ctx-size)
- `/status` — show server health, VRAM usage, active requests
- `/quit` — exit


### 2. Status and Dashboard (`tribunus ps` / `tribunus status`)

`tribunus ps` shows loaded models, active requests, VRAM usage, backend details, and uptime in a compact table:

```
MODEL                BACKEND    VRAM     TOKENS/S  REQUESTS  UPTIME
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
gemma-3-12b-it       Metal M1   11.2 GB   47.3      2        3h 12m
mistral-7b-v0.3      CUDA 4090   5.8 GB  112.1      0        14m
```

#### Verbose mode
`tribunus ps --verbose` adds per-model compilation evidence hash, arena page residency, ring buffer fill levels, speculative decode acceptance rate, active speculative tree width, KV cache compression ratio, and per-phase backend lane assignment.

#### Live dashboard
`tribunus status --watch` renders a live-updating terminal dashboard (refresh every 1s, like `htop`/`btm`):
- Per-model token throughput (instant + rolling 30s average)
- VRAM pressure gauge per backend
- Arena page allocation heatmap
- Ring buffer fill levels
- Active request queue depth
- KV cache utilization (compressed vs raw)
- Compilation evidence freshness indicator (current / stale)

#### Boot banner
On `tribunus serve` startup, print situational awareness banner:

```
tribunus 0.1.0 — inference server
  Machine: MacBook Pro M1 Max, 32 GB unified memory
  Backends: Metal (Apple M1 Max), ANE (16-core), Accelerate (CPU)
  Compute images: 3 ready (18.7 GB), 1 stale
  Listening on http://127.0.0.1:11434
```


### 3. Diagnostics (`tribunus doctor`)

`tribunus doctor` runs a comprehensive hardware and software readiness check. Designed to preempt 80% of support questions before they manifest as runtime errors.

#### Checks performed

| Check | Mechanism | Output on success | Output on failure |
|-------|-----------|-------------------|-------------------|
| OS version | `uname -a`, sw_vers | macOS 15.5 (Darwin 25.5) | — |
| CPU architecture | sysctl | Apple M1 (ARM64, 8+2 cores) | — |
| GPU detection | Metal API / vulkaninfo / nvidia-smi / rocm-smi | Metal M1 Max (32-core GPU), ANE (16-core) | No GPU detected: falling back to CPU |
| GPU driver version | Metal framework version / `nvidia-smi --query` | Metal driver 24.5 | GPU driver out of date (Metal 24.1 < required 24.5). Update: macOS System Settings → Software Update |
| Available VRAM | Metal heap size / `nvidia-smi` | 21.3 GB usable | — |
| Thermal throttling status | `pmset -g therm` | Normal (0% throttled) | Warning: CPU throttled at 45% (machine is hot). Close other apps or allow cooldown. |
| Disk space for model cache | statfs on `~/.tribunus/models` | 124 GB free on model volume | Low disk space: 2.1 GB free. Models may fail to download. Free at least 10 GB. |
| Backend binary availability | stat on `~/.tribunus/backends/*` | Metal (built-in), Accelerate (built-in) | Missing backends: CUDA (not on macOS — expected), Vulkan (not installed for this arch) |
| Network connectivity | HTTP HEAD to model registries | HuggingFace reachable (142 ms), Tribunus hub reachable (89 ms) | HuggingFace unreachable: check network or proxy settings. Models will not auto-download. Use `tribunus import <local-path>` instead. |
| Compute image integrity | SHA-256 verification on all cached images | 3/3 images verified | 1 compute image corrupted (sha256 mismatch). Run 'tribunus recompile <model>' to rebuild. |

#### Sample output

```
$ tribunus doctor
✓ OS: macOS 15.5 (Darwin 25.5) — Apple M1
✓ GPU: Metal (Apple M1 Max, 32-core GPU) — driver 24.5, 21.3 GB VRAM
✓ CPU: Not throttled (0% thermal pressure)
✓ Disk: 124 GB free on ~/.tribunus/models
✓ Backends: Metal, Accelerate built-in
✓ Network: HuggingFace (142 ms), Tribunus hub (89 ms)
✓ Compute images: 3/3 verified

All checks passed. The system is ready for inference.
```

#### Sample failure output

```
$ tribunus doctor --json
{
  "os": { "status": "ok", "detail": "macOS 15.5" },
  "gpu": { "status": "warn", "detail": "No GPU detected: falling back to CPU",
           "fix": "This machine has no Metal-compatible GPU. Running on CPU will be slow. Consider using an Apple Silicon Mac." },
  "thermal": { "status": "ok", "detail": "0% throttled" },
  "disk": { "status": "ok", "detail": "124 GB free" },
  "backends": { "status": "warn", "detail": "Missing: CUDA (not expected on macOS)" },
  "network": { "status": "ok", "detail": "HuggingFace: 142 ms" },
  "images": { "status": "ok", "detail": "3/3 verified" },
  "recommendation": "System can run inference but GPU acceleration is unavailable. Expected performance: ~1-2 tokens/s on CPU."
}
```


### 4. VRAM Estimation (`tribunus estimate <model>`)

Before downloading a model, `tribunus estimate <model>` calculates memory requirements per quantization level against the user's actual detected hardware and recommends the optimal variant.

```
$ tribunus estimate gemma-3-12b-it
Estimating memory requirements for gemma-3-12b-it on Metal M1 Max (21.3 GB usable)

Quantization    Weights    KV Cache (8K)  Scratch  Total     Fits?
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q4_K_M          7.8 GB     2.1 GB         0.3 GB   10.2 GB   ✓ (recommended)
Q5_K_M          9.1 GB     2.1 GB         0.3 GB   11.5 GB   ✓
Q8_0           12.5 GB     2.1 GB         0.3 GB   14.9 GB   ✓
fp16           24.8 GB     4.2 GB         0.6 GB   29.6 GB   ✗ (requires 8.3 GB more)

Recommendation: Q4_K_M — fits with 11.1 GB headroom for KV cache expansion up to 32K context.
Increase context to 16384 with Q4_K_M: +1.9 GB (12.1 GB total, still fits).
Decrease to Q3_K_S: 5.9 GB weights + 2.1 GB KV = 8.0 GB (minimal, but quality loss expected).
```

#### Error: Out of VRAM
```
Error: gemma-3-12b (Q8_0) requires 14.9 GB but only 8.1 GB available on Metal (M1).

Suggested fixes:
  1. Switch to Q4_K_M (7.8 GB) — best quality that fits
  2. Switch to Q3_K_S (5.9 GB) — minimal fit, some quality loss
  3. Reduce context to 4096 with Q8_0 to save 1.0 GB — still 5.8 GB over limit
  4. Unload another model: 'tribunus ps' to see loaded models, 'tribunus unload <model>' to free VRAM
  5. Run 'tribunus estimate gemma-3-12b-it' for all options
```


### 5. Model Details (`tribunus show <model>`)

`tribunus show <model>` reveals the compute image contents — which backends are targeted, per-phase assessment evidence (latency, GFLOPS), arena plan, and receipt from last compilation. This is Tribunus' key differentiator from every other inference server.

### 6. Configuration

Three-tier configuration model inspired by Caddy:

#### Tier 1: CLI flags (highest priority)
`tribunus serve --port 8080 --backend metal --ctx-size 8192 --verbose`

#### Tier 2: Environment variables
`TRIBUNUS_HOST`, `TRIBUNUS_PORT`, `TRIBUNUS_DEFAULT_BACKEND`, `TRIBUNUS_MODELS_DIR`, `TRIBUNUS_LOG_LEVEL`, `TRIBUNUS_KEEP_ALIVE`, `TRIBUNUS_MAX_LOADED_MODELS`. Every CLI flag has a corresponding env var.

#### Tier 3: Configuration file (lowest priority, but persistent)
A single `tribunus.jsonc` file (JSON with comments) at `~/.tribunus/config.jsonc` or `./tribunus.jsonc` (local path wins):

```jsonc
{
  // Served: server socket configuration
  "server": {
    "host": "127.0.0.1",
    "port": 11434,
    "keep_alive": "5m",
    "max_loaded_models": 3
  },

  // Backend: hardware backends to enable
  "backends": {
    "metal": { "enabled": true, "device": 0 },
    "cuda": { "enabled": false },  // not available on this machine
    "vulkan": { "enabled": false },
    "cpu": { "enabled": true, "threads": 4 }
  },

  // Cache: model storage and compilation policy
  "cache": {
    "models_dir": "~/.tribunus/models",
    "auto_pull": true,
    "recompile_on_driver_change": true,
    "max_cache_size": "100 GB"
  },

  // Models: per-model overrides
  "models": {
    "gemma-3-12b-it": {
      "quantization": "Q4_K_M",
      "backend": "metal",
      "ctx_size": 8192
    },
    "llama-3.1-8b-instruct": {
      "quantization": "Q8_0",
      "backend": "metal",
      "ctx_size": 4096,
      "speculative": {
        "draft_model": "llama-3.1-8b-draft",
        "tree_width": 8
      }
    }
  },

  // Logging
  "logging": {
    "level": "info",
    "format": "text",  // "text" | "json"
    "file": null
  }
}
```

#### Schema validation on startup
`tribunus.schema.json` is bundled with the binary. On startup, the config file is validated against the schema. Schema errors produce descriptive messages with line numbers.

#### Bridge command: effective config
`tribunus config show` prints the effective configuration (merged from defaults, config file, env vars, and CLI flags) as canonical JSON. `tribunus config validate` validates the config file without starting the server.

#### Verbose startup
With `--verbose`, Tribunus prints the effective config on startup, plus the detected hardware configuration and which config file was read:

```
$ tribunus serve --verbose
Config source: ~/.tribunus/config.jsonc (local: ./tribunus.jsonc not found)
Env overrides: TRIBUNUS_PORT not set, TRIBUNUS_LOG_LEVEL=debug
CLI overrides: --verbose

Effective configuration:
{
  "server": { "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 11434, "keep_alive": "5m", "max_loaded_models": 3 },
  ...
}
```


### 7. API Surface

Three categories of endpoints:

#### OpenAI-compatible endpoints (for SDK interoperability)

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| GET | `/v1/models` | List available models |
| POST | `/v1/chat/completions` | Chat completion (SSE streaming) |
| POST | `/v1/completions` | Text completion (SSE streaming) |
| POST | `/v1/embeddings` | Text embeddings |

Implementation follows the standard OpenAI schema for request/response bodies. Streaming uses Server-Sent Events. All endpoints respect the configured quantization and backend for the target model.

#### Tribunus management endpoints

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| GET | `/v1/tribunus/backends` | List available backends with capability flags and driver versions |
| GET | `/v1/tribunus/images` | List compute images with metadata |
| GET | `/v1/tribunus/images/:id` | Detailed image info (equivalent to `tribunus show`) |
| POST | `/v1/tribunus/compile` | Trigger compilation for a model; returns job ID for polling |
| GET | `/v1/tribunus/compile/:jobId` | Compilation status and progress |
| POST | `/v1/models/load` | Explicitly load a model into memory (`{"model": "gemma-3-12b-it"}`) |
| DELETE | `/v1/models/{name}/unload` | Explicitly unload a model, freeing VRAM |
| GET | `/v1/tribunus/arena` | Arena state (page allocation, ring buffer, KV cache pressure) |
| GET | `/health` | Health check with optional `?detail=1` for full runtime state |
| GET | `/v1/tribunus/metrics` | Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint |

#### Developer portals
- Swagger UI at `/docs` — auto-generated from OpenAPI schema. Non-negotiable. Every developer expects it.
- Chat playground at `/playground` — model selector, temperature/top-p sliders, system prompt editor, conversation history, "View as JSON" toggle, and a "cURL" tab that generates the equivalent curl command.


### 8. CLI Ergonomics

#### Verb-first command structure (Ollama-inspired)

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `tribunus serve` | Start the server (default foreground) |
| `tribunus run <model>` | Pull, compile, load, and start interactive chat |
| `tribunus pull <model>` | Download model weights (and optionally compile) |
| `tribunus compile <model>` | Explicitly compile a compute image |
| `tribunus list` | List installed compute images |
| `tribunus ps` | Show loaded models and resource usage |
| `tribunus show <model>` | Show model image details and compilation evidence |
| `tribunus rm <model>` | Remove a model and its compute images |
| `tribunus unload <model>` | Unload a loaded model from memory |
| `tribunus estimate <model>` | Show memory requirements per quantization level |
| `tribunus doctor` | Run system diagnostics |
| `tribunus search <query>` | Search model registries |
| `tribunus config show` | Print effective configuration as JSON |
| `tribunus config validate` | Validate configuration file |
| `tribunus version` | Print version and check for updates |
| `tribunus completion <shell>` | Generate shell completion script (bash/zsh/fish) |

#### Output conventions

| Property | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Default output | Human-readable table to stdout |
| Machine output | `--json` flag outputs JSON array/object to stdout |
| Errors | stderr only, with `Error:` or `Warning:` prefix |
| Progress | stderr — spinners for indeterminate, progress bars with ETA for determinate |
| Colors | Auto-detected (enabled when stdout is a TTY); green=ok, yellow=warn, red=error, cyan=info |
| Exit codes | 0=success, 1=error, 2=config error, 3=system check failed |
| Piped output | Colors disabled when stdout is not a TTY; `--json` recommended for pipes |

#### Shell completion
`tribunus completion bash` | `tribunus completion zsh` | `tribunus completion fish` — generates completion script to stdout. Users source it or redirect to their completion directory.


### 9. Error UX

Every error includes a 'fix' hint and follows the pattern: **what happened → why it happened → what to do next**.

| Scenario | Error message |
|----------|---------------|
| Model not found | `Error: model "unknown-99b" not found. Similar: mistral-7b (available), gemma-3-12b (installed). Run 'tribunus search unknown' to browse.` |
| Out of VRAM | `Error: gemma-3-12b Q8_0 needs 14.9 GB but 8.1 GB free. Try Q4_K_M (7.8 GB). 'tribunus estimate gemma-3-12b' for all options. 'tribunus unload' to free VRAM.` |
| Backend missing | `Error: CUDA backend not found. Detected NVIDIA RTX 4090 but CUDA 12.6 driver not installed. Install: 'sudo apt install nvidia-cuda-toolkit' or download from developer.nvidia.com/cuda-downloads. Fallback: 'tribunus serve --backend vulkan'.` |
| GPU not found | `Warning: No GPU detected for Metal backend. Detected GPUs: (none). This machine is running on CPU only. Commands are slow. Hardware requirements: Apple Silicon for Metal, NVIDIA GPU for CUDA, AMD GPU for ROCm.` |
| Stale compute image | `Warning: gemma-3-12b image compiled for driver 24.1, current driver is 24.5. Numerical oracle may have shifted. Run 'tribunus recompile gemma-3-12b' to rebuild.` |
| Corrupted image | `Error: gemma-3-12b compute image corrupted (sha256 mismatch). Run 'tribunus recompile gemma-3-12b' to rebuild.` |
| Download failed | `Error: download failed at 68% (connection lost). Resume with 'tribunus pull --resume gemma-3-12b'. Check network: 'tribunus doctor'.` |
| Config invalid | `Error: config.jsonc line 24: unknown key 'porrt' (did you mean 'port'?). Run 'tribunus config validate' for details.` |
| Port in use | `Error: port 11434 already in use by another process (PID 42069). Use --port to pick a different port: 'tribunus serve --port 11435'.` |
| Thermal throttling | `Warning: CPU/GPU thermal throttling detected (45% throttle). Inference may be slow. Close other GPU-intensive apps or allow the machine to cool down.` |


### 10. Cross-Cutting UX Decisions

#### Default to localhost-only
Bind to `127.0.0.1` by default. Exposing an inference server to the network requires an explicit flag: `tribunus serve --host 0.0.0.0` or env `TRIBUNUS_HOST=0.0.0.0`. This matches Ollama's security posture and prevents accidental exposure of a local inference endpoint to the LAN/WAN.

#### Auto-unload with configurable timeout
Unload idle models after a configurable keep-alive period (default 5 minutes). Show the remaining countdown in `tribunus ps`. This prevents VRAM waste while avoiding cold-start latency for active users. Configurable per-model in `tribunus.jsonc`.

#### First-run experience
On first launch, `tribunus serve` detects no models installed and prints:

```
  First run detected.
  No models installed. Try 'tribunus run gemma-3-12b-it' for a recommended starter model.
  Run 'tribunus doctor' to verify your system setup.
  Run 'tribunus search --popular' to see what's available.
```

#### Graceful shutdown
On SIGTERM/SIGINT: flush pending completion receipts, unload all models, release arena pages (freeing VRAM), save arena state to disk, and exit cleanly:

```
Shutting down...
  Flushing 2 pending receipts... done
  Unloading gemma-3-12b-it... freed 11.2 GB VRAM
  Unloading mistral-7b-v0.3... freed 5.8 GB VRAM
  Total 17.0 GB VRAM freed, 2 models gracefully unloaded.
  Bye.
```

#### Version and update notification
`tribunus version` shows the current version and checks for updates (opt-out with `--no-check`). If a new version with improved compilation quality or backend support is available, notify at startup but never block serving.

```
  A new version of Tribunus is available: 0.2.0 (you have 0.1.0)
  Update improves Metal kernel fusion for M3/M4 GPUs. Run 'brew upgrade tribunus' to update.
```

#### --json flag on all informational commands
Every command that returns structured data (`list`, `ps`, `show`, `estimate`, `doctor`, `config show`, `version`) supports `--json`. This enables scripting, monitoring integration, and composition with tools like `jq`.

#### Colored output convention
- Green (✓) — success, ready, current
- Yellow (!) — warnings, stale images, degraded performance
- Red (✗) — errors, failures, corrupted images
- Cyan/blue — informational headers, URLs, commands
- Auto-disable when stdout is not a TTY
- `--no-color` flag to force disable

#### Progress bars during model download and compilation
- Determinate phases (download, kernel benchmarking): progress bar (`██████░░ 68%`), transfer speed, ETA
- Indeterminate phases (memory planning, oracle validation): animated spinner with descriptive text
- Both render to stderr so pipes capture clean data
consequences:
### Positive
- **Zero-friction onboarding.** A single command (`tribunus run <model>`) gets a new user from zero to inference in one step, matching Ollama's industry-leading UX.
- **Differentiation through evidence.** No other inference server can display per-phase backend winners, numerical oracle agreement, or compilation evidence. This transforms server UX into a competitive moat.
- **Preemptive diagnostics.** `tribunus doctor` eliminates the top 80% of support issues (GPU detection, driver version, disk space, thermal throttling) before they become runtime failures.
- **Informed model selection.** `tribunus estimate` prevents VRAM out-of-memory errors at load time by showing users exactly which quantization fits their hardware before they commit to a download.
- **Developer interoperability.** OpenAI-compatible API + Swagger docs at `/docs` + playground at `/playground` means any OpenAI SDK works as a drop-in client without Tribunus-specific code.
- **Configuration clarity.** Three-tier model (CLI > env > config file) with `tribunus config show` bridge command eliminates "what config is actually active" confusion. Schema validation catches errors before the server starts.
- **Observability built in.** `tribunus ps --watch` live dashboard, Prometheus metrics, detailed `/health` endpoint, and arena state expose runtime behavior competitors hide.
- **Error UX that teaches.** Every error includes a 'fix' hint with the exact command to run. Users learn the tool through its error messages.
- **Scriptable by default.** `--json` flag on every informational command composes with `jq`, monitoring systems, and CI pipelines.
- **Builds on ecosystem conventions.** Adopts Ollama's verb-first CLI model, Caddy's configuration architecture, OpenAI's API surface, and LM Studio's VRAM estimation pattern. Users migrating from existing tools find familiar mental models.

### Negative
- **CLI surface area.** 16+ commands with `--json` flags on each adds implementation complexity. Each command needs: human table output, JSON output, progress indicators, error handling with fix hints, and shell completion entries.
- **Maintenance burden.** The `/health` endpoint arena state, the `tribunus show` evidence display, and the live dashboard all depend on runtime instrumentation (arena introspection, ring buffer sampling, per-phase latency counters) that must be built and maintained alongside the compiler.
- **Compilation evidence persistence.** `tribunus show` requires storing and querying compilation artifacts (assessment results, benchmark data, oracle certificates, memory plans) in a structured format. This is new storage — the compute image format must include a manifest section.
- **Config file evolution.** `tribunus.jsonc` schema must be versioned and migrated as features are added. Breaking changes to the schema require migration logic or compatibility adapters.
- **Playground maintenance.** A web playground at `/playground` introduces a frontend dependency (HTML/CSS/JS bundle) that must be updated alongside the API.
- **Shell completion generation.** Supporting bash, zsh, and fish means maintaining three completion generators or a shell-agnostic generator like `clap_complete`.
- **Localization not addressed.** Error messages and fix hints are English-only. Future work may need i18n for global adoption.

### Effort Estimate
3–4 weeks for CLI + API + status dashboard, assuming:
- Week 1: CLI scaffold (verb-first command tree, `--json` output, colors, progress bars, shell completion), `tribunus doctor`, `tribunus estimate`
- Week 2: API surface (OpenAI-compatible endpoints + management endpoints + Swagger), `/health`, `/playground`
- Week 3: Configuration model (`tribunus.jsonc`, schema validation, env var mapping, `config show`/`config validate`), `tribunus ps` table and `--watch` dashboard
- Week 4: `tribunus show` evidence display, error UX polish, first-run experience, graceful shutdown, version check

### Relationship to Existing ADRs
- ADR 0033–0035 (Prefill/Decode/KV Cache Runtime Pipelines) — the server UX surfaces instrumentation data from these runtime pipelines; `tribunus show` displays phase assignments that the runtime pipeline ADRs define.
- ADR 0036 (Scheduling and Arena) — `tribunus ps` /health display arena page residency and ring buffer fill levels that the scheduler ADR specifies.
- ADR 0037 (Backend Contract) — `tribunus show` lists backend winners per phase; `tribunus doctor` checks backend availability against the contract.
- ADR 0038 (Numerical Governance) — `tribunus show` displays oracle agreement and numerical tolerance; `tribunus ps --verbose` shows oracle certificate status.
- ADR 0039 (Speculative Decode) — `tribunus show` displays draft model config and acceptance rates from spec decoder pipeline.
- ADR 0040 (Output Streaming) — the SSE streaming in `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` is the wire protocol for output streaming.
